title: Database Indexing Strategies
description: Understand when and how to use database indexes effectively.

options.text: Adding more indexes always improves query performance
options.explanation: Indexes speed up reads but slow down writes — every INSERT/UPDATE must also update all indexes. Over-indexing can degrade overall performance.

options.text: A compound index on (A, B) can satisfy queries filtering on A alone but not B alone
options.explanation: Compound indexes follow the leftmost prefix rule. An index on (A, B) can serve queries on A or (A, B), but not B alone — B is only sorted within each A value.

options.text: B-tree indexes are ideal for full-text search
options.explanation: B-tree indexes are optimized for equality and range queries. Full-text search requires inverted indexes (like those in Elasticsearch or PostgreSQL's GIN indexes).

options.text: Covering indexes are indexes that span all tables in a database
options.explanation: A covering index includes all columns needed by a query, allowing the database to serve the query entirely from the index without accessing the table (index-only scan).
